question: A bid team on a Team plan is setting up a shared project for public-sector tender responses. Two writers will draft in it and four managers will review. Which two set-up choices are appropriate? Select two.
options: A) Paste the tender house rules at the top of each new chat instead of storing them.
B) Upload the approved boilerplate and the last three winning tenders as knowledge.
C) Have every writer make a personal copy of the project so nobody waits for anyone.
D) Ask an administrator to lift the five-project limit that applies to the bid team.
E) Share it with the two writers as "Can edit" and the four managers as "Can view".
correct_answers: B) Upload the approved boilerplate and the last three winning tenders as knowledge.
E) Share it with the two writers as "Can edit" and the four managers as "Can view".
explanations: House rules that apply to every bid are exactly what project instructions are for. Re-pasting them into each chat means they get shortened, misremembered or forgotten, and different writers end up working to different rules.

Correct. Project knowledge is where durable background belongs: uploading the boilerplate and past winning tenders makes that material available across every chat in the project, instead of being re-pasted per bid.

Personal copies destroy the shared context the project exists to provide: the separate knowledge bases drift apart, and every boilerplate update has to be repeated in each one. A shared project already lets people work at the same time.
The cap of five projects is a Free-account limit. This team is on a Team plan, which has no stated project limit, so there is no cap for an administrator to lift.

Correct, and on a separate axis from knowledge: this is the access decision. Project sharing is a Team and Enterprise capability, and the creator grants specific members either "Can view" or "Can edit" — those are the two levels that exist.
